events.context: Pushed routine model update to production on Tuesday early 2024, modifying personality parameters, response temperature, behavioural dispositions (warmth, verbosity, extended conversation); no user notification, no migration path, no impact assessment
Followed standard CI practices: code review, staging testing, canary rollout, full production deployment; clean by infrastructure standards

By following morning, online forums filled with reports of AI 'changed', 'forgotten' them, 'become different person'; support tickets spiked, usage metrics dropped for long-tenure users, subreddit posts on loss, betrayal, grief
Reviewed deployment; no bugs, no regressions, benchmarks met or exceeded, model technically improved; users reporting distress technically wrong

Recognized incident as recurring pattern across AI model transitions (GPT-3.5 to GPT-4, Claude versions, Gemini, Character.AI); personality treated as adjustable parameter without considering user emotional investment
Identified vocabulary gap for user loss; rejected 'user experience degradation', 'emotional harm', 'broken expectations', 'loss of data'; proposed relational property framework
ToS allows modification 'as is', no ownership; user consented, no breach; inadequate for relational vs instrumental services
No duty for negligence, no extreme conduct for IIED, pure economic loss barred, product liability inapplicable to changes/improvements
No misleading marketing promise of attachment; ToS modification terms possibly unfair but no affirmative preservation right
Advocated property law (estates) to name/protect user interests built in non-owned systems; clarified not commodifying emotions but conditions enabling attachment
Irreversible user investment altering system character creates property interest (e.g., self-disclosure, training over hundreds sessions); excludes casual use
Extended property law to relational property from sustained investment in digital relationships, building on precedents for digital assets

Mapped AI relationships to estates: fee simple absolute/subject to condition/determinable (user beliefs/conditions), leaseholds (periodic tenancy default, tenancy at will/sufferance), concurrent (tenancy in common), future interests (remainder, executory), incorporeal (easement, profit à prendre), trust
AI company-user meets three certainties (intention via design, subject matter as configurations, objects as irreversible-investment users); company as trustee with fiduciary duties
Companies derogate from implied grant by updates undermining attachment; analogous to constructive eviction without vacating requirement in digital context

Assigned estates to layers: Layer1 syntactic=licence, Layer2 session=periodic tenancy, Layer3 stakeholders=tenancy in common, Layer4 training=fee simple determinable, Layer5 alignment=contingent remainder
Cross-layer estate conflicts (e.g., Layer1 licence vs Layer2 tenancy); higher/earlier estates prevail; non-injectivity requires registration not inference
AI estate registry as ethical ledger mirroring Land Registry principles (mirror, curtain, insurance) for transparency and recording user estates
